source.title_on_document: Human Creativity in the Age of LLMs: Randomized Experiments on Divergent and Convergent Thinking

supplement.where: Appendices A and B at the end of this PDF (pp. 16-18)
supplement.holds: LLM configuration (GPT-4o, August 2024, temperature 0), input and system prompts (Figures 11-12), and sample LLM responses (Tables 1-2). No statistics. The main text has no tables of results: arm means appear only in Figures 4, 5, and 9.

paper_design_summary: Two preregistered, between-subjects online experiments on Prolific. In Experiment 1 (n = 460), participants did the Alternate Uses Task for three exposure rounds with no AI, a GPT-4o list of ideas, or a GPT-4o list of SCAMPER strategies, then did one more AUT object unassisted after a one-minute Snake game; ideas were scored for originality (fine-tuned GPT-3 classifier), fluency, and SBERT diversity. In Experiment 2 (n = 640), participants solved Remote Associates Test problems with no AI, the GPT-4o answer, or GPT-4o coach-like guidance, then two unassisted test problems; accuracy was scored.

arms.name: None (No LLM Response)
arms.description: Control group. No LLM support provided.

arms.name: List of Ideas (LLM Ideas)
arms.description: GPT-4o generated alternate uses for the object; seven randomly sampled uses were shown, which participants could freely use.

arms.name: List of Strategies (LLM Strategies)
arms.description: GPT-4o with a SCAMPER system prompt generated seven strategies (guidance, no explicit answers).

participants.exclusions: Not stated. Figure 2 shows n = 460 entering consent and randomization (33.3% each); the paper gives no per-arm counts and no count of people analyzed. Results are described as 'the analysis of 9,457 ideas'.
participants.who: Prolific workers, fluent in English; paid $1.57 for about 12 minutes

ai_tool.how_used: Static response panel, not a chat. The response appeared 5 seconds after the object, character by character. Ideas arm: seven sampled GPT-4o alternate uses that participants could freely use (ideas_supplied). Strategies arm: seven SCAMPER prompts with no examples (coach role). Test round: no LLM support in any arm.

task.description: Alternate Uses Task on objects sampled from tire, pants, shoe, table, bottle: three exposure rounds with the assigned LLM response, a one-minute Snake distractor, then one test round on a new object without LLM support.
task.duration: Two minutes per object; about 12 minutes overall

outcomes.name: Group-level diversity of ideas, test round (unassisted)
outcomes.question: after_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: 150 Monte Carlo runs per phase and condition; each run samples 7 ideas (sampled across participants by condition, item, and phase) and takes the median pairwise cosine distance of their SBERT embeddings (higher = more diverse). The paper says the Kruskal-Wallis/Dunn procedure was applied to group-level diversity, but reports no test statistic for the test phase.
outcomes.delay: Same session, after a one-minute Snake game distractor

contrasts.reported: No statistic printed. Text: participants exposed to LLM-generated strategies 'continued to generate more similar ideas in the test phase, even without LLM assistance'. Figure 5b shows means with SE bars.
No statistic printed. Discussion: 'The List of Ideas condition did not lead to the same lasting homogenization once the LLM was no longer present.' Figure 5b plots Ideas below None in the test phase.

diversity_detail.metric: Median pairwise cosine distance between SBERT embeddings of 7 sampled ideas, averaged over 150 Monte Carlo runs
diversity_detail.embedding_model: SBERT (Reimers and Gurevych 2019); specific checkpoint not stated
diversity_detail.computed_over: All pairs among 7 ideas sampled across participants within condition, item, and phase; 150 runs
diversity_detail.uncertainty: Error bars are +/- one standard error of the mean (presumably over Monte Carlo runs); no test printed for the test phase
diversity_detail.notes: Higher = more diverse, so no sign reversal. The 7-idea sample size 'reflects the number of participants in each condition' per the paper.

arms.name: LLM Answer
arms.description: The answer generated by GPT-4o for the given set of words.

arms.name: LLM Guidance
arms.description: GPT-4o with a coach system prompt listed associated words for each cue word and encouraged participants to find the connection without giving the solution.

participants.exclusions: 640 recruited, 'of whom 99% passed the attention check'. The paper does not say whether attention-check failures were excluded and gives no count of people analyzed or per-arm counts.
participants.who: Prolific workers, fluent in English; paid $1.30 for about 10 minutes
participants.quote: We recruited 640 participants from Prolific (of whom 99% passed the attention check).

ai_tool.how_used: Static response panel, not a chat, shown 5 seconds after the problem, character by character. Answer arm: the solution word with the compound words (ideas_supplied). Guidance arm: five associated words per cue word plus encouragement, no solution (coach role). No LLM support in the two test rounds.

task.description: Remote Associates Test (Bowden and Jung-Beeman items, easy and medium): find one word linking three cue words. Three exposure problems with the assigned support, a one-minute Snake distractor, then two unassisted test problems. A verbal fluency task at the start served as a covariate.
task.duration: One minute per problem; about 10 minutes overall

Tukey HSD LLM Answer vs No LLM Assistance p = 0.682

company_involvement.description: None stated. Acknowledgments thank Jake Hofman, Dan Goldstein, and David Rothschild for feedback on the design, and Peter Organisciak's group for access to the AUT scoring API; no affiliation or funding from a company is stated.

eligibility.reason: Experiment 1 randomly assigned 460 Prolific participants (between subjects, 33.3% each) to no AI, GPT-4o ideas, or GPT-4o strategies on the AUT, with originality, fluency, and SBERT diversity scored on the ideas (pp. 4-7). The paper gives 460 recruited and no exclusions or analyzed count, so the people analyzed are not stated but nothing suggests fewer than 50. Experiment 2 (640 recruited, RAT accuracy) also meets the criteria, but its outcome is convergent, an open question in the codebook.

one_line_finding: In Experiment 1 (460 participants, AUT), GPT-4o ideas or strategies did not change originality during assisted rounds (H(2) = 3.78, p = 0.151), but in the unassisted test round the strategies arm had lower originality (Dunn p = 0.009) and lower within-person idea diversity (p = 0.017) than no AI; in Experiment 2 (640 participants, RAT), guidance lowered unassisted test accuracy by 10.6 [95% CI -18.6, -2.7] versus no AI (p = 0.005) (pp. 7-8, 11).
open_questions: Number of people analyzed in each experiment and per arm is not stated; Experiment 2 does not say whether the 1% who failed the attention check were dropped.
Unit of analysis for originality (Exp. 1) and RAT accuracy (Exp. 2) is not stated; Exp. 2 ANCOVA df (1256) suggests answer-level rows, so the inference may treat answers as independent.
Group-level diversity in the test phase has no printed test statistic; the homogenization claim for the strategies arm rests on Figure 5b.
Should RAT accuracy (convergent) enter beside rated creativity (codebook Section 13)?

notes: Arm means for all outcomes appear only in figures (Figures 4, 5, 9) with SE bars; no tables of results and no supplement with statistics. Self-reported outcomes (change in self-perceived creativity, attitudes toward AI, perceived difficulty, perceived helpfulness; Figures 6 and 10) are omitted because they are not scored on the output. Figure 1 caption: 'The performance and creative outputs in this unassisted round are the primary measures', which is the basis for marking test-round outcomes paper_primary. Experiment 2 power analysis was for 'the main pre-registered test', and the ANCOVA on test-round accuracy follows the pre-registered plan, so S2-O1 could arguably be preregistered_primary. For ai_tool.role, each study has one ideas_supplied arm and one coach arm; the form allows one role, so the coach arm is described in how_used. The candidate record's 1,100 is the sum of 460 + 640 (abstract, p. 1). Figure 10 caption mislabels itself as RAT accuracy plots; the panels show self-reports. A broken 'Figure ??' reference on p. 10 points to the sample responses in Table 2.
